installation.note: nano is installed by default on most Linux distributions

overview.summary: nano is a simple, beginner-friendly text editor for the terminal. Unlike vim or emacs, nano is easy to use with on-screen help and intuitive keyboard shortcuts. It's perfect for quick file edits, configuration files, and beginners learning to edit files in the terminal.

syntax.description: Open FILE in nano editor. If FILE doesn't exist, nano creates it. Use keyboard shortcuts shown at bottom of screen.

misconceptions.title: nano is the same as vim
misconceptions.misconception: nano and vim work the same way
misconceptions.reality: nano is much simpler - you can type immediately, shortcuts are shown on screen, Ctrl+X to exit. vim has modes and is more complex.
misconceptions.tip: nano = simple, type and edit. vim = modes, more powerful but complex. Use nano for beginners, vim for advanced users.

misconceptions.title: nano requires special commands to type
misconceptions.misconception: nano has insert mode like vim
misconceptions.reality: nano works like a normal text editor - just start typing. No modes, no special commands needed. Arrow keys move cursor, type to add text.
misconceptions.tip: nano works like Notepad - just type. No modes or special commands needed to start typing.

common_pitfalls.issue: Not knowing how to save and exit
common_pitfalls.solution: Ctrl+O to save (Write Out), then Ctrl+X to exit. The shortcuts are shown at bottom of screen. ^ means Ctrl key.
nano will warn you if you try to exit with unsaved changes. Press Y to save, N to discard, or Ctrl+C to cancel.

related_commands.relationship: Text editor; nano is simple, vim is advanced
related_commands.description: Advanced text editor (more powerful but complex than nano)

related_commands.relationship: View files; cat to view, nano to edit
related_commands.description: Display file contents (nano edits, cat views)

best_practices: Use nano for quick edits and beginners
Use Ctrl+O to save (Write Out), Ctrl+X to exit
Use Ctrl+W to search within file
Use Ctrl+K to cut line, Ctrl+U to paste
Use sudo nano for system files
Read help at bottom of screen for shortcuts
performance_tips: Good for small to medium files
For very large files, consider vim or less

additional_notes.keyboard_shortcuts: Common: ^X (Ctrl+X) = exit, ^O (Ctrl+O) = save, ^W (Ctrl+W) = search, ^K (Ctrl+K) = cut line, ^U (Ctrl+U) = paste, ^ = Ctrl key
additional_notes.vs_vim: nano = simple, type immediately, on-screen help. vim = modes, more powerful, steeper learning curve.
additional_notes.beginner_friendly: nano is perfect for beginners - no modes, intuitive, help always visible
additional_notes.common_use: Very common: nano file.txt (edit), sudo nano /etc/file (system file), nano +10 file.txt (jump to line)
